items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: And Kenny Burrell went to it, Oliver Jackson.

ctx.x: Was there people in your high school even?

Oh yeah. Because it was a big area, my high school, Miller High School, that’s where I went, to Miller High School. It was the same school Bags went to, Milt Jackson went to that high school. And Kenny Burrell went to it, Oliver Jackson. Of course Detroit was a big area. It was very spread out. There must have been seven, eight, nine high schools there. Of course Tommy Flanagan went to a different one, Roland Hanna. Roland Hanna and Tommy went to the same high school. Barry Harris went to a different high school.…

items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Eddie Locke…I can’t think of his name right now, the other bop… It was another drummer that was Eddie Locke’s best friend.

ctx.x: Yeah, so it was cool. So I thank him, and I saw him later, you know, I used to see him. He’s passed on now, but I used to see him an always like Bags and Milt and Al would always thank him. My brother Billy went to that high school, he knew Billy. Yusef Lateef went there, his name was Bill Evans at the time, went to that same high school. Eddie Locke…I can’t think of his name right now, the other bop…
